newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Arsenic pollution a national crisis - minister.
newsitem.headline: Arsenic pollution a national crisis - minister.

text.p: Arsenic found in Bangladesh drinking water has created a "national crisis", Health Minister Salahuddin Yusuf said on Monday as worried residents called hospitals to find out how to avoid contamination.

"The crisis has created a panic in the country. I urge all concerned to use all their expertise and merit for its remedy," he told a seminar at Dhaka's Institute of Post-Graduate Medicine and Research (IPGMR) hospital.
The minister said tube-wells had been sealed off in many areas in view of possible poisoning of ground water.
"But the problem is that we have little alternate source of safe water," the official BSS news agency quoted Yusuf as saying.
Panic gripped residents in Dhaka after a newspaper on Sunday reported a finding of arsenic in a city suburb's water supply.
Doctors in Dhaka hospitals said they had received calls from people asking whether boiled water was safe from arsenic. "They want to avoid the deadly contamination," one doctor said.
Specialist doctors at Monday's seminar warned that arsenic pollution of sub-soil water was one of the worst health hazards Bangladesh has ever faced.
At least 126 arsenic patients have been treated since 1995 at the IPGMR alone, the hospital's chief dermatologist A. Z. M. Mayedul Islam said.

Although health officials in Dhaka did not confirm arsenic-related deaths, doctors in the northern district of Pabna said at least 11 people died after prolonged illness they believed was caused by arsenic poisoning. Hundreds are falling sick, Pabna doctors told reporters.
